declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes. Type formability prerequisites (closed and open u32 ranges, *mut, reference and nested non-null bases, slice pointers, the DispatchFromDyn prefix) were settled against rustc 1.98.0 on type-only files without any impl in obj/parallel/census-batch16/repro and obj/parallel/census-batch16/repro2. Each outcome follows the stated rule: a CoerceUnsized impl between two pattern types requires one identical pattern and then registers base_a: CoerceUnsized<base_b> as an ordinary obligation in the impl's environment; a struct pair requires its one changed field to satisfy CoerceUnsized; a DispatchFromDyn impl between two pattern types requires only one identical pattern; a coercion site selects Source: CoerceUnsized<Target>

core-pattern-coercion.rs.reason: core's exact pat.rs impl over the raw-pointer impls: the base obligation *const T: CoerceUnsized<*const U> holds by core's *const impl and the where-clause T: Unsize<U>

different-patterns.rs.reason: opponent: u32 is 1..=4 to u32 is 1..=8 has two different patterns, rejected before any base obligation

integer-base.rs.reason: opponent: the same pattern u32 is 1..=4 on both sides, but u32: CoerceUnsized<u32> has no impl (E0277)

pattern-to-pointer.rs.reason: opponent: a non-null pattern type to a plain raw pointer is neither a pattern pair nor a permitted pointer pair (E0376)

mutability-mismatch.rs.reason: opponent: *const T is !null to *mut U is !null; the base obligation *const T: CoerceUnsized<*mut U> has no impl (E0277)

mutable-to-const.rs.reason: *mut T is !null to *const U is !null; the base obligation holds by core's *mut T -> *const U impl

missing-unsize.rs.reason: opponent: core's impl without where T: Unsize<U>, so the base obligation's *const impl cannot prove T: Unsize<U> (E0277)

missing-pointer-impl.rs.reason: opponent: core's exact impl with no raw-pointer CoerceUnsized impl in the crate, so the base obligation *const T: CoerceUnsized<*const U> has no impl (E0277)

generic-base.rs.reason: impl<T: CoerceUnsized<U>, U> over T is !null; the base obligation T: CoerceUnsized<U> is the impl's own premise

reference-base.rs.reason: &'b T is !null to &'a U is !null with 'b: 'a; the base obligation holds by core's &'b T -> &'a U impl

nested-pattern.rs.reason: a non-null pattern over core's non-null raw pointer pattern; the base obligation is core's pat.rs impl itself

nominal-pattern-field.rs.reason: core NonNull shape: a repr(transparent) struct whose one changed field is *const T is !null implements CoerceUnsized through core's pat.rs impl

nominal-without-pattern-impl.rs.reason: opponent: the NonNull shape without core's pat.rs impl, so the changed field's CoerceUnsized obligation has no impl (E0277)

executed-coercion.rs.reason: a function body returns *const [u8; 4] is !null as *const [u8] is !null; the coercion site selects core's pat.rs impl and the builtin [u8; 4]: Unsize<[u8]>

dispatch-same-range.rs.reason: DispatchFromDyn between two u32 is 1..=4 pattern types: the same pattern, with no base obligation

dispatch-different-ranges.rs.reason: opponent: DispatchFromDyn from u32 is 1..=4 to u32 is 1..=8 has two different patterns
